open_points.subject: Registry read with an unsupported status
open_points.text: “a read whose project context would carry such a status is refused as an invalid Registry answer (the error it answers is that of the accepted `_authorize_project_operation` and its context model, carried to States 5–6)”
open_points.question: Which exact domain failure must a project read return when Registry reports `exists=true` with a status other than `active` or `archived`?
options: Return a Registry schema-mismatch boundary failure
Return an authorization/lifecycle rejection
Return another explicitly named typed failure

witness.initial: An authorized staff member has access to project P; Registry validation returns P with `exists=true` and status `paused`.
events: The staff member performs a project read.
The project guard tries to construct the authorized project context.
outcomes: The operation fails with a Registry schema-mismatch error.
The operation fails with a project lifecycle or authorization error.
witness.observer: The API caller and any HTTP error mapper see different error types and responses.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-001 verification binding
open_points.text: “PLAT-REG-001: a focused test at `validate_project_reference` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to PLAT-REG-001 and demonstrates that the portal never generates a Registry `project_id`?
options: Bind a check that attempts portal-generated project identity and proves refusal/no write
Leave PLAT-REG-001 without the required existing-check binding
open_points.default_guess: Add and bind a focused Registry identity check.

witness.initial: A generated implementation exposes a linked-write path that mints a UUID when no Registry project id is supplied.
events: A caller invokes that path.
The State 2 witness-resolution gate runs only the bindings currently listed for A5.
outcomes: A bound PLAT-REG-001 check rejects the implementation.
The current bindings do not exercise the path, so the implementation passes the gate.
witness.observer: The authoring gate and later users who see portal-created project identities.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-002 verification binding
open_points.text: “PLAT-REG-002: the ledger's property at `_validate_reference_identity` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to PLAT-REG-002 and proves linkage uses the returned UUID rather than display name or address?
options: Bind a property check with equal names/addresses and different UUIDs
Leave PLAT-REG-002 without the required existing-check binding
open_points.default_guess: Bind the named identity-validation property check.

witness.initial: Registry contains projects P1 and P2 with the same display name and address.
events: A linked write requests P1 but Registry returns P2.
The implementation matches by display name instead of UUID.
The currently listed A5 bindings run.
outcomes: A bound PLAT-REG-002 check detects the identity mismatch and fails.
The listed bindings do not exercise this mismatch and pass.
witness.observer: The authoring gate and the owner of P2's portal records.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-007 verification binding
open_points.text: “PLAT-REG-007: a focused test at `create_viewer` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to PLAT-REG-007 and proves a viewer's display name remains independent of Registry `customer_ref`?
options: Bind a create-viewer check with conflicting Registry customer data
Leave PLAT-REG-007 without the required existing-check binding

witness.initial: Registry project P has `customer_ref='C1'`; an administrator creates a viewer whose display name is `Family A`.
events: An implementation copies `customer_ref` into the viewer display name.
The currently listed A5 bindings run.
outcomes: A bound PLAT-REG-007 check fails because the viewer data was coupled to Registry data.
The listed bindings do not call `create_viewer`, so the coupling passes the gate.
witness.observer: The administrator and client see different viewer names.

open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-006 verification evidence
open_points.text: “PLAT-REG-006: a focused test at `get_project_context` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: What bound check actually calls the Registry gateway's `get_project_context` and proves live context is used instead of stored current truth while archived context remains read-only?
options: Bind a gateway-focused check that distinguishes live context from a stored snapshot and covers archived reads/mutations
Treat the guard and derived-view checks that substitute Registry calls as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Require a gateway-focused bound check; the supplied bindings only prove parts of archived behavior.

witness.initial: The portal previously observed project P as active with name `Old`; Registry now reports it archived with name `New`.
events: A caller reads P.
An implementation returns a locally stored `Old/active` context.
Both supplied PLAT-REG-006 checks run with Registry behavior substituted.
outcomes: A real `get_project_context` check fails because the live `New/archived` context was not fetched.
The supplied substituted checks pass without detecting the stored snapshot.
witness.observer: The caller sees stale project context and may be offered mutation behavior inconsistent with Registry.

open_points.subject: INV-020 snapshot immutability evidence
open_points.text: “INV-020: a focused test at `import_snapshot` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Must the bound check read back the accepted snapshot after a conflicting re-publication and prove that none of its content was overwritten or deleted?
options: Require read-back equality and retention of the original snapshot
Treat unchanged row counts and the conflict outcome as sufficient

events: The producer republishes the same identity with `approved_by='B'`.
A faulty import overwrites S in place but returns `integrity_conflict` and keeps the snapshot row count at one.
The supplied snapshot-import check runs.
outcomes: A read-back immutability assertion fails because S now contains `B`.
The supplied assertions pass because the outcome and row counts are unchanged.
witness.observer: A later reader of S sees altered supposedly immutable provenance.

open_points.subject: INV-022 producer activation prohibition
open_points.text: “INV-022: a focused test at `activate_budget_version` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: What assertion in the bound budget-management check proves that a producer has no activation capability and cannot activate its own import?
options: Exercise activation with a service-producer actor and prove refusal/no write
Infer producer prohibition from a staff capability check
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit producer activation refusal case.

witness.initial: A producer has just imported snapshot S, and its budget version V is inactive.
events: The producer invokes activation for V.
An implementation authorizes every authenticated importer to activate its own version.
The supplied budget-management check runs only staff contexts.
outcomes: An explicit producer case refuses activation and leaves V inactive.
The supplied check passes while the faulty implementation activates V.
witness.observer: The producer and project viewers see an unreviewed budget become active.

open_points.subject: INV-023 atomic budget activation
open_points.text: “INV-023: a focused test at `activate_budget_version` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: What bound scenario proves that failure after deactivating the old version but before completing activation rolls back the whole activation?
options: Inject a mid-activation persistence/audit failure and prove the former active version remains active
Treat precondition refusal and a successful switch as sufficient evidence of atomicity
open_points.default_guess: Require a mid-operation failure rollback test.

witness.initial: Project P has active version V1 and inactive version V2.
events: A caller activates V2.
The implementation commits V1's deactivation before writing V2's activation.
The second write fails.
outcomes: Atomic activation rolls back and V1 remains active.
Partial activation leaves both versions inactive.
witness.observer: Budget readers see either V1 or no active budget.

open_points.subject: INV-024 imported-plan immutability
open_points.text: “INV-024: a focused test at `upsert_manual_section_plan` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: How does the bound check prove that imported plans are immutable copies of their snapshot, not merely that manual plans and archived projects are handled correctly?
options: Attempt to edit an imported plan and prove refusal/no write while comparing it with snapshot content
Treat manual-plan cases as sufficient for the compound invariant
open_points.default_guess: Add an imported-plan edit refusal and snapshot-copy assertion.

witness.initial: Imported budget version V contains a plan copied from snapshot S.
events: A staff member calls the plan upsert using V's section.
A faulty implementation edits the imported plan.
The supplied check runs only the manual version's plans.
outcomes: An imported-plan case refuses the edit and preserves the copied values.
The supplied check passes while V is changed independently of S.
witness.observer: Budget readers see imported planned amounts that no longer match the accepted snapshot.

open_points.subject: INV-025 section linking evidence
open_points.text: “INV-025: a focused test at `_link_snapshot_sections` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Which assertion in the bound budget-management check invokes `_link_snapshot_sections` and distinguishes `source_key` matching from forbidden display-name matching?
options: Bind a check with equal names/different keys and equal keys/renamed sections
Treat unrelated manual-budget activation cases as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add and bind the explicit linking cases.

witness.initial: Existing section E has source key `K1` and display name `Kitchen`; a new snapshot section has key `K2` and the same display name.
events: A faulty linker reuses E by display name.
The supplied budget-management check runs without invoking the linker.
outcomes: A focused linking check requires a new section because the keys differ.
The supplied check passes while E is incorrectly reused.
witness.observer: Allocations and progress are silently attached to the wrong imported section.

open_points.subject: INV-026 verification binding
open_points.text: “INV-026: a focused test at `import_snapshot` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to INV-026 and proves actual expenses or mutable producer state cannot alter planned budget values outside snapshot import?
options: Bind an import/budget isolation check
Leave INV-026 without the required existing-check binding

witness.initial: Project P has a planned material amount of 100 and later records an actual expense of 30.
events: A faulty implementation rewrites the planned amount to 130.
The State 2 witness-resolution gate runs the currently listed A18 bindings.
outcomes: A bound INV-026 check fails because planned budget changed from actuals.
No binding names INV-026, so the faulty behavior is not checked as this invariant.
witness.observer: Budget viewers see planned values drift when expenses change.

open_points.subject: INV-027 verification binding
open_points.text: “INV-027: a focused test at `build_budget_view` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to INV-027 and proves totals and financial aggregates are recomputed rather than stored as editable values?
options: Bind a derived-view check that changes owning records and observes recomputation
Leave INV-027 without the required existing-check binding
open_points.default_guess: Bind the derived-view check explicitly to INV-027.

witness.initial: A project has stored plans totaling 100; a faulty implementation also stores an editable cached total of 100.
events: A plan changes to 120 without updating the cached total.
A budget view is built.
The witness-resolution gate sees no binding for INV-027.
outcomes: A recomputation check expects 120 and fails on the cached value.
The invariant has no bound check and the stale total can pass the gate.
witness.observer: Budget viewers see a stale total of 100 instead of 120.

open_points.subject: INV-028 verification binding
open_points.text: “INV-028: a focused test at `PortalTransaction.commit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to INV-028 and attempts to delete a section referenced by an allocation or progress record?
options: Bind a commit-level referential-protection check for both reference kinds
Leave INV-028 without the required existing-check binding

witness.initial: Section S is referenced by an expense allocation.
events: A faulty transaction deletes S and commits.
The currently listed A18 bindings run.
outcomes: A bound INV-028 check refuses the commit and preserves S.
No binding names INV-028, so the orphaning behavior is not exercised as this invariant.
witness.observer: Expense readers encounter an allocation whose section no longer exists.

open_points.subject: INV-033 changed witness binding
open_points.text: “INV-033: a focused test at `_build_replacement_allocations` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing. Witness: `replace_expense_allocations` with the explicit amounts 150.00 to a section and 50.00 to other expenses persists exactly those two allocations, and a replacement of 1.00 against the 200.00 total is refused with `ExpenseValidationError` while the stored row counts stay unchanged; nothing spreads an amount”
open_points.question: Does the bound check's delegated support code actually assert exact persistence of 150.00 and 50.00 and no-write refusal of the 1.00 replacement?
options: The support code contains all stated exact-value, exception, and unchanged-row-count assertions
The support code only exercises a multi-allocation replacement or lacks one or more stated assertions
open_points.default_guess: Do not accept the binding until the delegated support content is available and verified.

witness.initial: The named check consists only of a call to delegated support code whose content is not supplied.
events: An implementation spreads or rewrites the explicit 150.00/50.00 amounts, or writes before rejecting the 1.00 mismatch.
The named wrapper check runs.
outcomes: If the delegated support contains the newly claimed assertions, the check fails.
If it merely exercises replacement without those exact assertions, the same faulty implementation passes.
witness.observer: The State 2 decision-witness gate cannot distinguish the two outcomes from the supplied binding content.

open_points.subject: INV-050 verification binding
open_points.text: “INV-050: a focused test at `build_project_overview` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to INV-050 and compares repeated results for the same accepted inputs to demonstrate deterministic recomputation?
options: Bind a repeated-build check with identical owning records and dependency answers
Leave INV-050 without the required existing-check binding

witness.initial: Owning records and external answers are unchanged between two overview reads.
events: A faulty builder uses iteration order or ambient randomness when composing a result.
The witness-resolution gate runs with no check bound to INV-050.
outcomes: A repeated-build assertion detects different results.
Without a binding, both individually valid-looking results pass the invariant gate.
witness.observer: The client sees the overview change between identical reads.

open_points.subject: INV-052 append-only evidence
open_points.text: “INV-052: a focused test at `PortalTransaction.commit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.”
open_points.question: Where does the bound snapshot-import check attempt to mutate or delete an existing import record and an existing audit record and prove commit refusal with no changes?
options: Add commit-level mutation and deletion attempts for both record types
Treat duplicate insertion, rollback, and accumulating rows as sufficient evidence of append-only storage
open_points.default_guess: Require explicit mutation/deletion refusal for both import and audit records.

witness.initial: A classified import has import record I and audit record A.
events: A faulty repository exposes an update that changes I's outcome and deletes A.
A transaction commits those changes.
The supplied snapshot-import check runs only inserts, duplicate-key failures, rollbacks, and reads.
outcomes: A commit-level append-only check refuses the transaction and preserves I and A.
The supplied check passes because it never attempts either mutation or deletion.
witness.observer: The producer sees altered import history and auditors lose the corresponding audit fact.
